title: Fix the List Modification While Looping
description: The program should remove all negative numbers from a list. Fix the bug.
expectedBehavior: The program should print [3, 5], with every negative number removed.
actualProblem: Removing an item from a list while iterating over it with a for loop shifts the remaining elements left, and the loop's internal position advances past whatever slides into the vacated spot. Here, removing -1 shifts -2 into index 0, but the loop moves on to index 1 next, so -2 is skipped and survives in the final list — [-2, 3, 5] instead of [3, 5].
correctedCode:
numbers = [-1, -2, 3, 5]
numbers = [n for n in numbers if n >= 0]
print(numbers)
explanation: Mutating a list (adding or removing elements) while iterating over it directly leads to skipped or repeated elements, because the loop's internal index doesn't account for the shift. Building a new filtered list (e.g. with a list comprehension) avoids the problem entirely.
